# package gsdx

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/gsdml/gsdx"
```

Package gsdx inspects GSDX containers: Open Packaging Conventions (OPC) packages, ISO/IEC 29500-2 / Ecma-376 Part 2, which are public.

It is a generic, safe container inspector. It reads the ZIP under strict limits (part count, per-part and total uncompressed size, compression ratio), rejects hostile part names, and reports the package model: the parts with their content types, the package and part relationships, the core properties, the metadata of the OPC digital signatures and the parts that look like GSDML documents. WriteTo re-emits every part unchanged.

What it does not do: the GSDX Container Specification of PROFIBUS & PROFINET International (PI order 2.752), its signing policy and MRCD are published to PI members only. This package applies no PI-specific rule, never says that a file is a valid GSDX, and does not verify signatures: see Signature. Rules of OPC itself that a package breaks without being dangerous to read are reported as Issues, not as errors.

Clause references are to the requirement titles of Ecma-376 Part 2 (Open Packaging Conventions); their numbers differ between editions.

## Constants

```go
const (
	DefaultMaxParts     = 4096
	DefaultMaxPartSize  = 64 << 20
	DefaultMaxTotalSize = 256 << 20
	DefaultMaxRatio     = 200
	// RatioFloor is the uncompressed size under which the compression
	// ratio is not checked: small runs of repeated text compress far
	// beyond any sensible ratio without being a threat.
	RatioFloor = 64 << 10
)
```

Default limits of Options. They are generous for a device description (a GSDML file is at most a few MB) and small enough that a hostile file cannot exhaust memory.

## Functions

### func IsGSDML

```go
func IsGSDML(part *Part) bool
```

IsGSDML reports whether a part looks like a GSDML document: its content type names GSDML, or its file name follows the GSDML naming convention ("GSDML-...xml"). The content type PI's GSDX specification assigns is members-only, so this is a heuristic, not a rule of that specification.

### type DigestCheck

```go
type DigestCheck string
```

DigestCheck is what Open found when it compared the digest of a part reference with the part.

```go
const (
	// DigestNotChecked: the reference has transforms (canonicalization
	// or the relationship transform, not implemented), an unknown digest
	// method, or no part to compare with. DigestNote says which.
	DigestNotChecked DigestCheck = "not-checked"
	// DigestMatch: the digest over the part's octets equals DigestValue.
	DigestMatch DigestCheck = "match"
	// DigestMismatch: the part changed after it was signed, or the
	// DigestValue is wrong.
	DigestMismatch DigestCheck = "mismatch"
)
```

The outcomes of a digest comparison.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(r io.ReaderAt, size int64, opts Options) (*Package, error)
```

Open reads the package from r. It returns an error wrapping profinet.ErrMalformed for input that is not a ZIP, has no \[Content\_Types].xml, has a part name that is absolute after mapping, contains a "." or ".." segment, an empty segment or a backslash, or two entries whose names are equal ignoring ASCII case; and profinet.ErrResourceExhausted when a limit of opts is exceeded. Every entry is decompressed and its CRC-32 checked.

OpenFile opens the package in the file at path with the default Options.


#### func (Package) WriteTo

```go
func (p *Package) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (int64, error)
```

WriteTo writes the package as a ZIP: every entry in its original order, with its name, compression method, modification time, comment and content unchanged, so that nothing is lost by opening and writing a package. The compressed octets may differ from the input's: entries are compressed again.

### type Signature

```go
type Signature struct {
	Part                   string `json:"part"`
	ID                     string `json:"id,omitempty"`
	CanonicalizationMethod string `json:"canonicalizationMethod,omitempty"`
	SignatureMethod        string `json:"signatureMethod,omitempty"`
	// SignedInfoReferences are the references of ds:SignedInfo.
	SignedInfoReferences []Reference `json:"signedInfoReferences,omitempty"`
	// PartReferences are the references of the ds:Manifest elements.
	PartReferences []Reference `json:"partReferences,omitempty"`
	// SignatureTime and SignatureTimeFormat are the OPC SignatureTime
	// signature property, as written; empty when absent.
	SignatureTime       string        `json:"signatureTime,omitempty"`
	SignatureTimeFormat string        `json:"signatureTimeFormat,omitempty"`
	Certificates        []Certificate `json:"certificates,omitempty"`
	// Verified is always false; Reason says why.
	Verified bool   `json:"verified"`
	Reason   string `json:"reason"`
}
```

Signature is the metadata of one OPC digital signature (Ecma-376 Part 2, "Digital signatures"): a signature part reached from the Digital Signature Origin part through a signature relationship.

Signatures are NOT verified. Verifying one needs XML canonicalization (C14N) of SignedInfo and of the package-specific Object, the OPC relationship transform, the check of the SignatureValue with the signer's key, and a trust decision on the certificate, which for a GSDX follows PI's members-only signing policy. None of that is implemented: Verified is always false and Reason says why.

What Open does compare is narrower: for a part reference of the Manifest that has no ds:Transforms, the digest over the part's octets. XML Signature (W3C XML Signature Syntax and Processing, "Reference Processing Model") digests the octet stream the URI dereferences when no transform applies, and OPC signatures are XML signatures whose part references dereference the part's content. A DigestMatch says that this part is the one that was digested; it does not say that the signature is valid, since the Manifest itself is covered only by the unverified SignatureValue.
